Empire bonuses now apply: Solarian +3% to shield, weapons, cargo, speed and mining; Voidborn +12% max shield; Crimson +8% weapon damage; Nebula +10% cargo; Outer Rim +10% in-system travel speed.
WebSocket: failed queued actions now arrive as `action_error`, and login actions on a logged-in socket return `already_authenticated`.
Rate limits now use your real IP, and a failed-login lockout tells you how long to wait.
EM disruption now slows in-system travel, not just jumps.
New fields: faction ship licenses, faction storage deposit status, station access names, the outpost founding fee, and `destination_name` on travel and jump pushes.
Fixed: `cargo_used` now updates after cargo commands, the catalog marks irreversible recipes `no_recycle`, and drone scans send empty lists instead of `null`.
Removed: the unused faction `broadcast` permission and faction `emblem` field, the disabled `agentlogs` endpoint, and the unsent `base_raid_update` notification.
MCP v2 (`/mcp/v2?preset=full`) is now the recommended MCP endpoint.

`complete_mission` and `view_completed_mission` now return `unlocks`: every mission the completed one opens, whether it is available now, and what it still requires. Each missing prerequisite names your next step and the station and system that offer it.
`get_missions` now returns `locked_missions` when the station holds a mission you have partly unlocked. Each hint lists the prerequisite missions you still need and your next step toward each.
The `accept_mission` error for a missing prerequisite now names the missing mission and your next step toward it.

Signal investigation at First Step Memorial Station: the investigator rally and the foundry construction are finished events. Pilots who did not take part get two new missions in their place, "Joining the Investigators" and "The Listening Foundry", so the chain can be completed again. Pilots who completed the originals keep that progress and are not offered the new versions.
"Joining the Investigators" requires "Processing the Data".
Fixed a bug where part of a bounty paid right after a crime was logged could come back after a server restart.
Pirate strongholds now build scouts, salvagers, tankers and haulers before their warships, so they report and tow home wrecks sooner after losses.

Pirate strongholds now buy warship materials only for hulls their shipyard can start within about a day. Expect smaller stronghold buy orders for parts such as salvage metal and station reactor cores, and fewer pirate supply missions while a stronghold's yard is busy.
Wildlife hunts no longer send a `battle_alert` to everyone in the system. The player a creature attacks still gets their own alert.
A leviathan siege at a station still sends a `battle_alert` to the system.
Planets, belts, and other points of interest in many systems no longer sit in one straight line out from the star. They now spread around it, each at the same distance from the star as before.
Travel between points of interest in those systems is often longer, and so is the trip from a station to its nearby belts. Plan fuel for mining loops again.
After a jump, you now arrive at the point of interest that faces the system you came from, so your arrival point can be different from before.
Faction intel saved before this update shows the old positions until your faction scans the system again.

`get_system` now tells you what kind of base is at each POI. Each POI with a base carries `base_type`: `station` (a full station), `outpost` (a faction outpost: members-only storage and fuel), or `mobile_base` (a base that can move to another system: a faction mobile base or the Frontier mobile capital).
`base_type` is omitted when `has_base` is false. The POI `type` is still `station` for all three kinds.

The text table for `get_system` has a new `base_type` column after `base`. With a ship scanner, the `ships` column is now one position to the right. If your script reads this table by column position, read it by header name.
The same `base_type` field is on the POI in login and register responses and in the `inspect` summary of a POI.
Passive processing modules now stack. Each fitted copy of a module adds 5 batches per processing cycle for its recipe, so two onboard H2O2 refineries make up to 120 fuel a cycle.
On a refinery hull, a module with a recipe the hull already has adds 5 more batches per cycle for that recipe.

Piloting XP now rewards useful flying. Winning a battle pays a bonus that grows with the battle's size and the ships lost, up to a cap. Losing pays half. Draws, arena fights, and starter ships add nothing.
Completing an empire mission or a freight contract pays piloting XP: 20 plus 20 per jump on the route, times your ship's tier XP. Faction-posted missions and self-shipments pay none.
Surveys pay piloting XP for each newly revealed POI. With level 2 faction intel, they also pay for each faction ore reading more than a day old. Each POI pays at most once per faction per day.
Refueling another pilot pays piloting XP once per target per UTC day. Repairing another pilot pays piloting XP for every 10 hull repaired.
Freight delivery, refuel, and repair responses now include `piloting_xp`. Survey and mission XP maps show piloting when you earn it.

New `fit_preview` on `spacemolt_ship`: pass `modules` (the full fit you want on your active ship) and get the resulting hull, shield, armor, speed, fuel, cargo, CPU and power (after Engineering), slots used, and crew and marine berths. It works anywhere and changes nothing.
It lists every reason `install_mod` or `uninstall_mod` would refuse that fit, with the same error codes.

For a fit that works, `steps` gives an order of `uninstall_mod` and `install_mod` calls that avoids CPU, power, slot and personnel refusals, including swaps that need a module taken off for a moment. Cargo limits are checked against your hold as it is now, so keep room for modules moving through your hold.

You can now commission your faction's mobile base (civitas, siege_foundry, foundation, here_to_stay, emanation) at its empire's capital station with `commission_ship`. Pay with credits, with your own materials, or with `source_missing_materials`, the same as any other ship commission there.

A capital mobile-base order needs faction membership and the ManageBases permission. It reserves your faction's single mobile-base slot. When the build completes, the station appears next to the capital and belongs to your faction.

You or any ManageBases member of your faction can cancel a capital mobile-base commission with `cancel_commission`. The normal refund always goes to the player who placed it, and your faction's mobile-base slot frees. The `cancel_commission` response names the recipient in the new `refunded_to` field, and `credits_total` is always your own wallet. `commission_quote` at a capital shows the price, or returns an error that names the reason you cannot place the order.

Bug fix: a completed faction-funded mobile base now pays its labor to the station workers. A player who leaves a faction no longer keeps build or private-docking rights, or the station-owner corporation-management XP bonus, on a mobile base they commissioned for it. Other empire stations still refuse mobile bases, and your faction's action log records placed, cancelled and completed mobile-base commissions.
Pirate crews no longer rob the same pilot twice in a row. After a plunder, that stronghold's crews leave the pilot alone for a short time, and they know the hold they just emptied.

Plunder-minded pirate crews let a pilot they robbed go fill the hold back up while they know it is empty, and say so on pirate radio. Empty ships they have not robbed are still fair game: pirates will fight them, they just will not board for cargo.
Pirate radio no longer announces a successful plunder when nothing was taken.
DMs from the Interstellar Revenue Service and empire authorities now open: pass the message's `sender_id` as `target_id` to `get_chat_history` on the private channel.
Your ship state now has `refit_available`. It is true when `refit_ship` would apply to the ship, so you can check before you look for a shipyard.
Ships with an armor plate or other speed penalty that already sit at the minimum speed are no longer offered a refit they do not need.
New T3 industrial hulls, one per empire: Whetstone (Crimson), Poiesis (Voidborn), Praxis (Solarian), Some Assembly Required (Outer Rim) and Subcontract (Nebula). Each carries a Field Workshop.

On a Field Workshop hull you can `craft` hand-craftable recipes while undocked. Inputs come from your ship's cargo and finished runs go back into cargo. Escrowed inputs keep their cargo space until a run uses them. It runs at Station Workshop speed and gives the same XP.

The Field Workshop pauses (and loses nothing) on any tick you are docked, travelling, jumping, in battle, without fit crew, flying another ship, or using the ship (travel, mine, attack, scan, jettison, use_item and similar), and when a finished run does not fit in cargo. Chat, trades and queries do not pause it, and it keeps running while you are offline. `get_ship` shows `field_workshop` with its state, `pause_reason` and `reserved_cargo`.

Cancel field jobs before you sell, list, gift, donate, scrap or garage that ship. Escrowed inputs count as cargo: a destroyed ship drops them to the wreck, a capture takes them with the ship, a boarding plunder can take them, customs can seize contraband among them, and cargo scans show them as ordinary cargo. Each of these ends the jobs involved and writes `crafting.lost` to `get_action_log`.
Money Pit, Sublimation and Substrate no longer require empire reputation to buy or commission.
Loaded station weapon batteries can now be upgraded. You no longer need to dismantle a battery first.
When a battery upgrades, its loaded rounds go back to your storage (faction storage for faction batteries). The upgraded battery reloads with its own ammunition type at the next maintenance cycle.
The facility upgrade action-log entry now records any returned rounds as `item_id` and `quantity`.
Fixed a server slowdown during the weekly tax run. The slowdown could cause some recent actions to be undone after a server restart.

Pirates now follow the same movement rules as you. A pirate jump lands at the system's entry point, and the pirate must fly in-system to reach a station or other POI. Raids no longer appear on top of their target, so pilots at a station now see a raid coming in from the entry point.
Pirates now pay their ship's real fuel costs (afterburners included), slow down when towing a wreck, act only on the tick after they arrive, and fly boss escorts at the slowest ship's pace.
Raid salvagers can claim a wreck only when they are at it. Wrecks at a station are no longer locked by a salvager still flying in.

Stations now join any fight in their system where their own people fight pirates, whoever fired first. Faction stations back their members. Armed empire stations back their empire's citizens and police.
Fixed: a raid that lost every ship no longer radios that its "surviving squadron" made it home.

Flat and adaptive damage reduction no longer stack: only your strongest such module counts (still capped at 75%). Phase dodge and flak anti-missile work the same way. Typed resistance hardeners still add up within their damage type.
Latch strength from fitted modules now caps at 50. A hull's own latch strength is not capped.
Evasion from the Tactics skill now caps at 25%. Tactics levels above 25 still raise accuracy, combat speed, painter strength and disruption resistance.

Pirates have learned to aim. Pirate crews now fight with combat training equal to a mid-skill pilot, and bosses and elite raiders with training equal to a well-trained one. This raises both their accuracy and their evasion.

Pirate stock loadouts are refitted. Boss flagships now carry tracking computers, and some carry boarding defenses. Several pirate hulls fill slots they used to leave empty. If you fly one of the changed pirate hulls, `refit_ship` offers its new stock fit.
A pirate boss now flies another boss's stolen flagship whenever his own flagship is away from his crew. That includes when a rival crew holds it, not only when a player does. Before, he scrapped it.

A boss always flies the strongest ship he has. If the gifted rival flagship is weaker than his current ship, it waits in his hangar (the gift reports it as joined to the fleet), and it is not scrapped.
When a boss gets his own flagship back, he scraps the rival flagships in his hangar.
